title: The 24-Hour Internal Clock Inside Your Body
summary: Discover how natural 24-hour oscillations regulate biological processes, and how external cues like light keep our internal clocks synchronized.
evidenceNote: While the core 24-hour endogenous oscillations and their regulation by the suprachiasmatic nucleus are well-established, the precise functional importance of certain specific clock genes like CLOCK continues to be studied.

scenes.text: What tells your body when to sleep, wake, and eat every single day?
A circadian rhythm is a natural oscillation that repeats roughly every 24 hours inside living organisms.
As early as the 4th century BC, observers noted that certain plants close their leaves at night and open them at sunrise.
These rhythms are endogenous, meaning they originate within the organism and persist even without external cues.
External cues like light and temperature, called zeitgebers, adjust these internal rhythms to the local environment.
Your internal clock coordinates biological processes to match the solar day.
